newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSTANT VIEW-Australian balance of goods/services.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-Australian balance of goods/services.

text.p: Australia's seasonally adjusted balance of trade and services posted a surplus of A$336 million in February, compared with median expectations of a A$13 million deficit, and a revised A$38 million deficit in January.
Forecasts had ranged widely, from a A$200 million deficit to a A$250 million surplus.
A selection of economists immediate reactions to the data follows.
MICHAEL BLYTHE, SENIOR ECONOMIST, COMMONWEALTH BANK OF AUSTRALIA:

"On the goods and services side, obviously, it was a good result. I think it just highlights that the goods and services balance is going to be just as hard to forecast as the monthly current account figures were. It does suggest that we've got off to a reasonably good start for the March quarter current account."
ANNETTE BEACHER, SENIOR ECONOMIST, CITIBANK AUSTRALIA:

"The wild card was exports and the exports have come in in our favour. What we have seen for the last couple of months is a strong take-on from the rural side and maybe this has continued for another month. A positive trade balance will help the current account, but no matter what the trade balance gives us it is overwhelmingly swamped by our net income deficit."
CHRIS CATON, CHIEF ECONOMIST, BANKERS TRUST AUSTRALIA:

"The trade data looks good on the face of it. Markets haven't really adjusted to this new method of presentation. But the surplus is a good result. It does remind people that we ring our hands about Australia's foreign trade performance, but the new way of presenting it does remind people that we sell as much to the rest of the world as we buy from it. And the current account deficit is dominated by the net income deficit. The current account deficit will probably still get bigger this year than it was last year, but that's because growth is going to pick up. The job figures are still consistent with a slowly improving labour market."
